`437312` (Bleeding) is the SNOMED ancestor. Now the final staged query: cancer + VTE patients with LMWH-before-DOAC, and 90-day post-switch inpatient bleeding admissions, grouped by DOAC.

arguments.sql_query:
WITH doac AS (
  SELECT descendant_concept_id AS concept_id, ancestor_concept_id AS doac_ing
  FROM omop.concept_ancestor
  WHERE ancestor_concept_id IN (43013024,40241331,45892847)
),
lmwh AS (
  SELECT descendant_concept_id AS concept_id
  FROM omop.concept_ancestor
  WHERE ancestor_concept_id IN (1301025,1301065,1308473)
),
cancer_vte AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT co.person_id
  FROM omop.condition_occurrence co
  JOIN omop.concept_ancestor ca ON ca.descendant_concept_id = co.condition_concept_id
  WHERE ca.ancestor_concept_id IN (444247,440417)
    AND co.person_id IN (
      SELECT DISTINCT co2.person_id FROM omop.condition_occurrence co2
      JOIN omop.concept_ancestor ca2 ON ca2.descendant_concept_id = co2.condition_concept_id
      WHERE ca2.ancestor_concept_id = 438112)
),
lmwh_start AS (
  SELECT de.person_id, MIN(de.drug_exposure_start_date) AS lmwh_start
  FROM omop.drug_exposure de JOIN lmwh ON lmwh.concept_id = de.drug_concept_id
  WHERE de.person_id IN (SELECT person_id FROM cancer_vte)
  GROUP BY de.person_id
),
doac_start AS (
  SELECT de.person_id, d.doac_ing, MIN(de.drug_exposure_start_date) AS doac_start
  FROM omop.drug_exposure de JOIN doac d ON d.concept_id = de.drug_concept_id
  WHERE de.person_id IN (SELECT person_id FROM cancer_vte)
  GROUP BY de.person_id, d.doac_ing
),
switchers AS (
  SELECT ds.person_id, ds.doac_ing, ds.doac_start
  FROM doac_start ds JOIN lmwh_start ls ON ls.person_id = ds.person_id
  WHERE ds.doac_start >= ls.lmwh_start
),
first_doac AS (
  SELECT person_id, doac_ing, doac_start,
         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY person_id ORDER BY doac_start) AS rn
  FROM switchers
),
cohort AS (
  SELECT person_id, doac_ing, doac_start FROM first_doac WHERE rn = 1
)
SELECT c.doac_ing, cc.concept_name AS doac,
       COUNT(DISTINCT c.person_id) AS n_switchers,
       COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN b.person_id IS NOT NULL THEN c.person_id END) AS n_with_bleed_admit
FROM cohort c
JOIN omop.concept cc ON cc.concept_id = c.doac_ing
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT DISTINCT vo.person_id, vo.visit_start_date
  FROM omop.visit_occurrence vo
  JOIN omop.condition_occurrence co ON co.visit_occurrence_id = vo.visit_occurrence_id
  JOIN omop.concept_ancestor ca ON ca.descendant_concept_id = co.condition_concept_id
  WHERE vo.visit_concept_id IN (9201,262)
    AND ca.ancestor_concept_id = 437312
) b ON b.person_id = c.person_id
     AND b.visit_start_date >= c.doac_start
     AND b.visit_start_date <= c.doac_start + INTERVAL '90 day'
GROUP BY c.doac_ing, cc.concept_name
ORDER BY n_switchers DESC;

content.text:
What the failures told me:
- The DB is **SQL Server** and the tool is **strictly read-only/single-SELECT** — no `INTERVAL`, no `SELECT ... INTO #temp`, no multi-statement scripts.
- The full CTE cohort join (cancer ∩ VTE ∩ LMWH→DOAC ∩ 90-day bleed) is too heavy and times out at 600s. My assumption that I could do it in one pass is wrong.

New approach: keep each query to a single SELECT, and shrink the working set aggressively. The DOAC-switcher counts I already have are the bottleneck's cause. Let me get the switcher cohort size per DOAC first (cancer+VTE + LMWH-before-DOAC), pushing filters down and avoiding the bleed join.

arguments.sql_query:
SELECT ds.doac_ing, COUNT(*) AS n_switchers
FROM (
  SELECT de.person_id, d.doac_ing, MIN(de.drug_exposure_start_date) AS doac_start
  FROM omop.drug_exposure de
  JOIN (SELECT descendant_concept_id AS concept_id, ancestor_concept_id AS doac_ing
        FROM omop.concept_ancestor
        WHERE ancestor_concept_id IN (43013024,40241331,45892847)) d
    ON d.concept_id = de.drug_concept_id
  GROUP BY de.person_id, d.doac_ing
) ds
JOIN (
  SELECT de.person_id, MIN(de.drug_exposure_start_date) AS lmwh_start
  FROM omop.drug_exposure de
  JOIN (SELECT descendant_concept_id AS concept_id
        FROM omop.concept_ancestor
        WHERE ancestor_concept_id IN (1301025,1301065,1308473)) l
    ON l.concept_id = de.drug_concept_id
  GROUP BY de.person_id
) ls ON ls.person_id = ds.person_id AND ds.doac_start >= ls.lmwh_start
WHERE ds.person_id IN (
  SELECT co.person_id
  FROM omop.condition_occurrence co
  JOIN omop.concept_ancestor ca ON ca.descendant_concept_id = co.condition_concept_id
  WHERE ca.ancestor_concept_id IN (444247,440417)
  INTERSECT
  SELECT co.person_id
  FROM omop.condition_occurrence co
  JOIN omop.concept_ancestor ca ON ca.descendant_concept_id = co.condition_concept_id
  WHERE ca.ancestor_concept_id = 438112
)
GROUP BY ds.doac_ing
ORDER BY n_switchers DESC;

content.text: I have the switcher cohort. Now I need the 90-day bleed admissions per DOAC. To avoid timeout, let me define the cohort inline but only join bleed events, keeping it a single SELECT. I'll restrict bleed to inpatient/ER visits within 90 days of each patient's first qualifying DOAC start.

arguments.sql_query:
SELECT c.doac_ing,
       COUNT(*) AS n_switchers,
       SUM(CASE WHEN c.has_bleed = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS n_with_bleed_admit
FROM (
  SELECT ds.person_id, ds.doac_ing, ds.doac_start,
    CASE WHEN EXISTS (
      SELECT 1 FROM omop.visit_occurrence vo
      JOIN omop.condition_occurrence co ON co.visit_occurrence_id = vo.visit_occurrence_id
      JOIN omop.concept_ancestor ca ON ca.descendant_concept_id = co.condition_concept_id
      WHERE vo.person_id = ds.person_id
        AND vo.visit_concept_id IN (9201,262)
        AND ca.ancestor_concept_id = 437312
        AND vo.visit_start_date >= ds.doac_start
        AND vo.visit_start_date <= DATEADD(day,90,ds.doac_start)
    ) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS has_bleed
  FROM (
    SELECT dq.person_id, dq.doac_ing, dq.doac_start,
           ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY dq.person_id ORDER BY dq.doac_start) AS rn
    FROM (
      SELECT de.person_id, d.doac_ing, MIN(de.drug_exposure_start_date) AS doac_start
      FROM omop.drug_exposure de
      JOIN (SELECT descendant_concept_id AS concept_id, ancestor_concept_id AS doac_ing
            FROM omop.concept_ancestor
            WHERE ancestor_concept_id IN (43013024,40241331,45892847)) d
        ON d.concept_id = de.drug_concept_id
      GROUP BY de.person_id, d.doac_ing
    ) dq
    JOIN (
      SELECT de.person_id, MIN(de.drug_exposure_start_date) AS lmwh_start
      FROM omop.drug_exposure de
      JOIN (SELECT descendant_concept_id AS concept_id
            FROM omop.concept_ancestor
            WHERE ancestor_concept_id IN (1301025,1301065,1308473)) l
        ON l.concept_id = de.drug_concept_id
      GROUP BY de.person_id
    ) ls ON ls.person_id = dq.person_id AND dq.doac_start >= ls.lmwh_start
    WHERE dq.person_id IN (
      SELECT co.person_id FROM omop.condition_occurrence co
      JOIN omop.concept_ancestor ca ON ca.descendant_concept_id = co.condition_concept_id
      WHERE ca.ancestor_concept_id IN (444247,440417)
      INTERSECT
      SELECT co.person_id FROM omop.condition_occurrence co
      JOIN omop.concept_ancestor ca ON ca.descendant_concept_id = co.condition_concept_id
      WHERE ca.ancestor_concept_id = 438112
    )
  ) ds
  WHERE ds.rn = 1
) c
GROUP BY c.doac_ing
ORDER BY n_switchers DESC;

content.text: The bleed join across all cancer+VTE+switcher patients still scans too much. The cohort is small (5,142 total switchers) but the recomputation of the whole cohort CTE plus the visit/condition join is the cost. Let me reduce scope: compute bleed numerator for **one DOAC at a time**, starting with apixaban, and narrow the DOAC ingredient filter so the planner has less to expand.

arguments.sql_query:
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT c.person_id) AS apixaban_bleed_admit
FROM (
  SELECT dq.person_id, dq.doac_start
  FROM (
    SELECT de.person_id, MIN(de.drug_exposure_start_date) AS doac_start
    FROM omop.drug_exposure de
    JOIN (SELECT descendant_concept_id AS concept_id
          FROM omop.concept_ancestor WHERE ancestor_concept_id = 43013024) d
      ON d.concept_id = de.drug_concept_id
    GROUP BY de.person_id
  ) dq
  JOIN (
    SELECT de.person_id, MIN(de.drug_exposure_start_date) AS lmwh_start
    FROM omop.drug_exposure de
    JOIN (SELECT descendant_concept_id AS concept_id
          FROM omop.concept_ancestor WHERE ancestor_concept_id IN (1301025,1301065,1308473)) l
      ON l.concept_id = de.drug_concept_id
    GROUP BY de.person_id
  ) ls ON ls.person_id = dq.person_id AND dq.doac_start >= ls.lmwh_start
  WHERE dq.person_id IN (
    SELECT co.person_id FROM omop.condition_occurrence co
    JOIN omop.concept_ancestor ca ON ca.descendant_concept_id = co.condition_concept_id
    WHERE ca.ancestor_concept_id IN (444247,440417)
    INTERSECT
    SELECT co.person_id FROM omop.condition_occurrence co
    JOIN omop.concept_ancestor ca ON ca.descendant_concept_id = co.condition_concept_id
    WHERE ca.ancestor_concept_id = 438112
  )
) c
WHERE EXISTS (

## Mechanistic framing (what the pharmacology predicts, independent of the query)

This part I can answer from established pharmacology — treat it as hypothesis, to be confirmed against the numbers above:

- **Target/pathway.** LMWHs act indirectly via antithrombin, accelerating inhibition of **factor Xa** (and some IIa). The oral DOACs split into two mechanisms:
  - **Direct factor Xa inhibitors** — apixaban, rivaroxaban, edoxaban.
  - **Direct thrombin (factor IIa) inhibitor** — dabigatran (absent here).
- **Why bleeding risk differs among the Xa inhibitors** despite a shared target:
  - **Dosing schedule / peak-trough.** Apixaban is **twice-daily**, giving lower peak plasma concentrations and flatter exposure; rivaroxaban is **once-daily** with higher peaks — higher Cmax is associated with more mucosal/GI bleeding.
  - **GI luminal exposure.** Rivaroxaban has lower, more variable oral bioavailability with more active drug transiting/absorbed distally, correlating with higher **GI bleeding** signals; apixaban has less local GI anticoagulant effect.
  - **Renal clearance.** Rivaroxaban ~35% renal, edoxaban ~50%, apixaban ~27% — in cancer patients with fluctuating renal function and nephrotoxic chemo, higher renal dependence raises accumulation/bleeding risk.
  - **P-gp / CYP3A4 interactions.** All three are **P-glycoprotein** substrates; apixaban and rivaroxaban are also **CYP3A4** substrates (edoxaban minimally). Azole antifungals, some tyrosine-kinase inhibitors, and other oncology drugs inhibit these pathways and raise DOAC levels.
- **Prior RCT/real-world signal (context, not from this DB):** In cancer-associated thrombosis, rivaroxaban and edoxaban (SELECT-D, Hokusai-VTE Cancer) showed **more bleeding — especially GI/GU — than dalteparin**, whereas apixaban (Caravaggio) did **not** show a significant excess of major bleeding. The consistent prediction is therefore **fewer 90-day bleeding admissions on apixaban** than on rivaroxaban, driven mainly by twice-daily flatter pharmacokinetics and lower GI luminal exposure.
